FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.94
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` does not evaluate fixes in a real sandboxed project context. In `bench/endocrine.py`, it copies only the target file into a temp directory (`patched_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, os.path.basename(target_path))`) and then runs pyright/ruff/bandit against that lone file. For tests, it runs the provided `test_cmd` with `cwd=tmpdir` but does not rewrite the command to point at copied tests, and does not copy the rest of the source tree at all. Evidence: any fix whose correctness depends on sibling modules, package-relative imports, config files, or actual test files will be evaluated against an incomplete filesystem, so “sandbox-test proposed fixes” is not actually happening for the project.
FOLLOW: This crosses the endocrine↔immune interface because `immune_agents.run_immune_pipeline()` imports `evaluate_fixes()` and marks findings `verified=True` when verdict is SAFE or NEUTRAL. With the current setup, project-level breakage can be missed: a patch may look SAFE on an isolated file while breaking imports/integration in the real codebase. Conversely, valid fixes can be marked HARMFUL or UNEVALUABLE because tests and package context are absent. That corrupts the bug-closed gate, dedup, and escalation logic downstream by causing false verification or false rejection of fixes.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — copy the minimal project context into the tempdir before evaluation: at least all `source_paths`, preserving relative layout, and if `test_cmd` is provided ensure referenced test paths exist inside the tempdir before running it there. Then run pyright/ruff/bandit/tests against the copied sandbox paths, not the original file path.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.88
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.52
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` can mark a harmful fix as SAFE because `_compute_fix_verdict()` collapses all tool deltas into one signed sum: `total_net = net_type_errors + net_ruff_errors + net_bandit_issues`; if `total_net > 0` => HARMFUL, if `< 0` => SAFE. Evidence: a fix that introduces one new Bandit issue (`+1`) while removing two Ruff issues (`-2`) yields `total_net = -1` and is classified SAFE even though it introduced a new security defect. The same masking applies across tool classes generally.
FOLLOW: This directly affects the fix-verification contract consumed by `immune_agents.run_immune_pipeline()`, which treats SAFE/NEUTRAL as sufficient to set `verified=True`. A patch that regresses security or typing but improves style can be promoted to verified, after which NK bug-closed logic may suppress future reports of the still-broken bug. That creates silently wrong reviewer output, not just noisy metrics.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — treat any positive individual delta (`net_type_errors > 0` or `net_ruff_errors > 0` or `net_bandit_issues > 0`) as HARMFUL; only classify SAFE when no category increased and at least one category improved or tests passed.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.84
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.47
DESCRIPTION: FIND — baseline and post-fix tool counts in `evaluate_fix()` are not measured on equivalent code layouts. Pre-fix counts are gathered on `target_path` in the real repository, while post-fix counts are gathered on an isolated temp file `patched_path` with a different path/package context. For tools that resolve imports or config relative to project structure, these counts are not comparable. Evidence: pyright and even lint/security tooling can change findings based on path, package root, and neighboring files; a delta computed from different environments is not a valid before/after comparison.
FOLLOW: The verdict engine assumes these deltas reflect the effect of the patch. Because they do not, SAFE/HARMFUL/NEUTRAL can be wrong in either direction. Downstream this pollutes `fix_evaluations`, can incorrectly set `verified=True` in the immune pipeline, and makes endocrine’s headline capability “sandbox-test proposed fixes” misleading to the insect brain and human reviewer.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — compute both pre-fix and post-fix counts inside the same temp sandbox: copy the sandbox project once, run tools before patching on the sandbox copy, apply the patch there, then rerun tools on the same sandbox path.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004
SEVERITY: 0.76
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.34
DESCRIPTION: FIND — the module advertises CrossHair-based fix evaluation/analysis but CrossHair is dead code. `CROSSHAIR_BIN` and `_CROSSHAIR_TIMEOUT` are declared, `ToolDiagnostic.tool` docstring lists `"crosshair"`, and the module docstring advertises the binary, but there is no `run_crosshair()` and no call site in `scan_health()` or `evaluate_fix()`. This feature never fires.
FOLLOW: The health scan capability exposed to the rest of the system is overstated. Human reviewers and the insect brain may assume symbolic execution contributes to health signals or fix safety when it does not. In PoC terms this is misleading output rather than a crash, but it directly affects trust in the endocrine report.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — remove CrossHair from the advertised tool list and related constants until a runner is actually wired into `scan_health()`/`evaluate_fix()`.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F005
SEVERITY: 0.73
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.31
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `scan_health()` silently drops tool-failure information from totals and counts, so parse failures/timeouts look like a clean scan. Evidence: each runner returns `[]` on `NOT_FOUND`, and on JSON parse failure logs a warning then returns an empty diagnostics list; `_run_tool()` also maps timeout to returncode -1/stderr "TIMEOUT". `scan_health()` aggregates only diagnostics, with no failure counters except a misleading `tools_available` bool already covered in registry. A timeout or malformed output therefore produces `total=0` for that tool, indistinguishable from “no issues found.”
FOLLOW: The insect brain receives a `HealthScan` that can underreport defects during tool failure windows. Combined with inter-round decision-making, this can suppress health deterioration signals and make a broken scanning round appear healthier than the previous one. It also undermines fix evaluation baselines because `_count_tool_issues()` similarly returns `0` on exceptions, biasing verdicts toward SAFE/NEUTRAL.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — add per-tool execution status/failure counts to `HealthScan` and, in fix evaluation, propagate tool execution failure as UNEVALUABLE instead of treating it as zero issues.
VERIFIED: TRUE

EXTEND C0005 | endocrine.py also advertises CrossHair support that never fires: `CROSSHAIR_BIN`, `_CROSSHAIR_TIMEOUT`, and ToolDiagnostic docs mention crosshair, but there is no runner or call site in scan_health/evaluate_fix. This is another concrete dead advertised capability, not just unused defect categories.

EXTEND C0001 | tool failure is also flattened to “zero issues” in fix evaluation via `_count_tool_issues() -> 0 on exception`, so missing/broken tools can make proposed fixes look SAFE/NEUTRAL and feed false `verified=True` into the immune pipeline.
